project: PRD-266 W1 Connect — Automatos Go backend: discovery, the mobile_devices table, device pairing and the device lane, remote access, editors answer, chat and voice for the phone (one branch, one PR, one CI run)
description: PRD-266 (docs/PRDS/PRD-266-AUTOMATOS-GO-BACKEND.md) wave W1 (Connect): US-001..US-008 re-cut into 16 stories that each fit one session, in dependency order (K2). Backend + web; ONE Alembic revision (prd266_mobile_devices); no new dependency; no third-party client. The PRD is in the base (the docs branch of PR #1257). Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd266w1.sh --print-base`.
decisions: D1 (PRD-266 §3, Gerard 20 Oct): v1 editions are SaaS + open-source pairing. Enterprise (a customer-owned Clerk instance found at runtime) and the enterprise proof of concept are after WebSummit [D2].
D5–D6 (§3): sign-in only; Clerk email code, password and passkey. No social logins, so no Sign in with Apple.
D63 (§3, revises D7): the app deletes nothing. Deleting a workspace stays in Studio, unchanged; a person who wants their login removed asks support [D47].
D8 (§3): billing shows nothing on the phone. No change here.
D13 (§3): Gerard's VPS demo install is the WebSummit server: HTTPS on a domain, API and web published, datastores private.
D15 (§3): 'Report this' goes to the workspace owner and an Automatos moderation inbox; on a self-hosted install to its operator only (W3: not this wave).
D16 (§3): editors may answer questions and grant or deny tool approvals; viewers may not; applies to the web too (US-006a, US-006b).
D18–D19 (§3): lock screen Open and Answer on an unlocked phone; Face ID before approve is client-side only. NO server step-up.

D20–D23 (§3): push carries a question's text and options, everything else generic; self-hosted servers push through Expo after the operator agrees at pairing; three push types; a one-time AI consent sheet names the providers (W2/W3: not this wave).
D24 (§3): the daily digest is Auto's Read, posted as Auto's message at each user's chosen time (W2: not this wave).

D32–D34 (§3): Auto Live joins Retell's call natively (LiveKit React Native SDK), so the mint passes Retell's transport fields through; quick-ask voice uses spokenMode; Live is Business-only on SaaS (US-007a, US-008a).
D39 (§3): a native marker in the azp check, landed before #1216 merges (US-020, outside the waves: not this kit).
D53 (§3): Retell audio retention off, transcripts kept, EU region if offered (the Retell dashboard: human-gated, not code).

§4.2: ONE new table mobile_devices, not an extension of cli_hosts (cli_hosts registers CLI runtimes: capabilities, heartbeats, terminals, sessions, local only; a phone carries a person, push credentials and digest preferences; mixing the lifecycles makes every query branch on kind). Hashing, code alphabet, TTL and one-time token return come from the kernel extracted from services/cli_host_service.py; rotation keeps the previous token valid for 10 minutes.

§4.3: the device lane (Bearer amd_…) is resolved BEFORE the Clerk lane and ONLY when AUTH_EDITION=local; in saas an amd_ token is 401. The UserContext is built from the bound users row; workspace_id is bound to the row (a different X-Workspace-ID is 403); raw_claims carry {source: 'mobile_device', device_id, user_id}; last_seen_at is written at most every 5 minutes.

§4.3: identity is a CREDENTIAL, NEVER AN ADDRESS. Inside the container a request from the same machine and one from the LAN can both arrive from the Docker gateway, and a same-host reverse proxy makes every caller look like 127.0.0.1: no code trusts a source address for identity.

§4.3 + §11 open question 1 (unanswered on 20 Oct, so the PRD's default ships): FAIL CLOSED. A local install whose API or web app is published beyond loopback with LOCAL_REMOTE_ACCESS=off refuses to boot with a message naming the fix; LOCAL_REMOTE_ACCESS=open keeps today's behaviour and logs a warning at every boot; paired closes the anonymous lane (401 device_pairing_required).
§4.1/§4.3: the QR payload is a UNIVERSAL LINK https://<web_url>/go/pair?api=<api_url>&code=<code>, NEVER a custom scheme (any app can register a scheme).
§4.1: discovery carries names and capabilities only, never secrets; the app gates every feature on capabilities, never on a version number; capabilities list only what this build implements.

§4.10 where code goes: new code in new modules: core/auth/pairing.py (the shared kernel), core/auth/bearer_registry.py (the bearer-prefix registry, called once before the Clerk lane), core/auth/device.py (resolve_device_context), core/models/mobile_devices.py (the core/models/cli_hosts.py pattern), the package services/mobile/ (pairing.py, devices.py, discovery.py, remote_access.py; one domain, one package, as services/themes/), thin routers api/mobile_devices.py and api/well_known.py (validate with Pydantic, call the service, map errors; plain def over the sync session), api/chat_models.py (ChatRequest moved out of api/chat.py, then spokenMode); core/auth/workspace_admin.py gains require_workspace_answerer and api/approval_grants.py only swaps the dependency; web in components/settings/phones-devices/ with hooks in hooks/use-mobile-devices.ts, calls only through lib/api-client.ts; tests orchestrator/tests/test_prd266_<area>_<what>.py and frontend *.test.tsx beside the component.

§4.10 files already over AGENTS.md's 800-line limit may NOT grow: core/auth/hybrid.py (954), api/chat.py (908), api/approval_grants.py (806), main.py (1,681), services/cli_host_service.py (2,799); also every other over-800 file this wave touches (consumers/chatbot/service.py 3,074, frontend/lib/api-client.ts 3,847). They gain only a call or an import and, where that would grow them, something moves out in the same commit. The one named exception: orchestrator/config.py gains its settings lines (AGENTS.md: settings live only there), and the generated reports route-manifest.json and config-surface.json gain their entries.

§4.10 code shape on every changed line: functions under 50 code lines, nesting under 4, cyclomatic complexity under 10, new files 200–400 lines (never over 800), type hints and docstrings on public functions, no mutation of arguments, no swallowed errors; settings only through config.py with each name in reports/config-surface.json (no os.getenv/os.environ elsewhere, ruff TID251); no hardcoded values (named constants or config).

§4.10 AGENTS.md exception 1 (approved by Gerard 20 Oct; this wave's PR records it): TWO PUBLIC ROUTES, GET /.well-known/automatos.json and POST /api/v1/mobile/pair, against 'every new endpoint is authenticated', as PRD-264 D16 did for /verify. Discovery carries names and capabilities only; /pair is rate-limited (per IP and per instance) and code-gated.
§4.10 AGENTS.md exception 2 (approved 20 Oct): one third-party client, services/push/expo.py. It is W2's: this wave adds NO third-party client and NO new Python or npm dependency.

§4.10 'stop and ask first' record (#1253, approved by Gerard 20 Oct): authentication (the device lane; remote-access mode closing the anonymous lane), permissions (editors answer: this reverses PRD-196's owner/admin posture, on the web too), tenancy (device rows and tokens bound to one workspace; a different X-Workspace-ID is 403).

§4.11 enterprise alignment (PRD-257): ONE pairing kernel (core/auth/pairing.py) for CLI hosts, phones and next PRD-257's estate runners; ONE credential registry (core/auth/bearer_registry.py): phones add amd_, runner and workload-identity tokens add a resolver later, never another branch in hybrid.py; discovery reserves OIDC (v1 never emits an 'oidc' mode; the schema stays automatos-discovery/v1 when it is added); device rows carry kind, so an OIDC-signed phone becomes a third kind, not a new table; nothing here chooses PRD-257's open question 4.
§8: a clerk device row never holds a token hash; a paired row never exists on SaaS. Tests cover both edges.

A Next.js server surface that calls the API without the browser's headers (the themes files proxy, the root layout's theme boot fetch) either reads the token from a SameSite=Strict cookie set beside it, local edition only and read only on the Next.js server side, or degrades to the base theme without an error; the DONE mark names each surface and the choice.

The per-instance bucket is the brute-force ceiling (8 characters from a 32-symbol alphabet, alive 10 minutes).

userStories.description: As a self-hoster, I want to mint a pairing code from Studio and have my phone exchange it for a device token, so it can reach my install without a login system (PRD-266 §4.3, US-003).
acceptanceCriteria: New package orchestrator/services/mobile/ (__init__.py, pairing.py, and a small urls helper for api_url/web_url per K15): create_pairing_code(db, workspace_id, user_pk) adds a PENDING mobile_devices row (kind paired, pairing_code_hash, pairing_expires_at = now + PAIRING_CODE_TTL_SECONDS) and returns {code, expires_at, qr_payload}; pair_device(db, code, name, platform, app_version, install_id) activates a valid, unexpired, unused pending row (status active, install_id, name, platform, app_version, paired_at, token_hash from mint_token('amd_', …), events gains 'enrolled', last 50 kept) and returns the token ONCE with rotate_after = paired_at + MOBILE_TOKEN_ROTATE_DAYS; an unknown, expired or used code returns None. A phone that pairs again (same workspace, user and install_id) ends with exactly ONE row (the unique constraint holds; say which row survives in the DONE mark). Alphabet, TTL, hashing and minting come only from core/auth/pairing.py. → DONE — orchestrator/services/mobile/ (new): __init__.py; pairing.py: create_pairing_code(db, workspace_id, user_pk, *, request_base_url) → PairingCode(code, expires_at, qr_payload) adds a PENDING kind-paired row (pairing_code_hash, pairing_expires_at = now + PAIRING_CODE_TTL_SECONDS) after deleting the caller's own expired pending codes (review finding); pair_device(db, code, name, platform, app_version, install_id) → PairedDevice(device_id, workspace_id, token, rotate_after) or None: the code is looked up by digest FOR UPDATE, compared with secrets_match and must be unexpired; the row goes active with install_id, name, platform, app_version, paired_at, last_seen_at, token_hash from mint_token('amd_', 32), the code and any previous token cleared, events + 'enrolled' (services/mobile/events.py with_event keeps the newest 50, as a new list); rotate_after = paired_at + MOBILE_TOKEN_ROTATE_DAYS. urls.py holds api_url/web_url (K15; HOSTED_PUBLIC_API_HOST is a module constant in config.py and PUBLIC_API_HOST's default). WHICH ROW SURVIVES a re-pair: the phone's EXISTING row for (workspace, user, install_id) keeps its id and takes the new token, name/platform/version (a revoked row is active again, its history kept plus 'enrolled'); the new code's pending row is deleted. A code holder acts as the person who minted it, so naming another of that person's install_ids re-pairs that phone (security review, accepted). Judgement call: the extra keyword request_base_url carries K15's request base URL (the AC's signature has no request). Alphabet, TTL, hashing, minting and compare come only from core/auth/pairing.py. Saas raises PairingUnavailable (§8). commit d3eeb1aa5

POST /pair — PUBLIC (AGENTS.md exception 1, named in the module docstring), 404 unless AUTH_EDITION=local AND LOCAL_REMOTE_ACCESS=paired; body {code, name, platform, app_version, install_id} validated (platform ios | android | web; install_id 8–128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; name ≤ 120) → {device_id, workspace_id, token, rotate_after}; a wrong, expired or used code → 401 {"code": "invalid_pairing_code"} and nothing more. → DONE — orchestrator/api/mobile_devices.py (new; plain def routes; Pydantic PairRequest). POST /pair: PUBLIC, named in the module docstring as AGENTS.md exception 1; dependencies=[_require_paired_mode (404 unless AUTH_EDITION=local AND LOCAL_REMOTE_ACCESS=paired), limit_pair_attempts_per_ip]; body validated (platform in MOBILE_DEVICE_PLATFORMS ios|android|web; install_id ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}$; name ≤ 120; app_version ≤ 32; code ≤ 32) → {device_id, workspace_id, token, rotate_after}, no-store; a wrong, expired or used code → 401 with detail {code: invalid_pairing_code} (the repo's HTTPException detail-dict shape) and nothing more. Rate limits (K13, revised by the lead 20 Oct): /pair checks a per-IP bucket only, BEFORE the code (a named operation in core/security/rate_limiter.py DEFAULT_LIMITS through config.rate_limit_for, e.g. mobile_pair_ip, or the api/provenance.py RateLimitStore pattern; reuse, never a third limiter); over it → 429 with Retry-After. There is NO per-instance bucket: an 8-character code from a 32-symbol alphabet with a 600 s lifetime cannot be guessed at any rate the API serves, and a shared bucket would let one caller block pairing for everyone. A wrong code costs that caller one attempt and never invalidates the pending code. The async limiter runs in an async DEPENDENCY so the route itself stays a plain def. → DONE — DEFAULT_LIMITS['mobile_pair_ip'] = config.rate_limit_for('mobile_pair_ip', 10, 600) in core/security/rate_limiter.py, counted per IP with the api/provenance.py RateLimitStore pattern (the AC's second option, chosen after the code review flagged check_rate_limit's sync Redis on the event loop): limit_pair_attempts_per_ip is a plain def dependency, so the Redis round trip runs in the threadpool and the routes stay plain def; fail-open logs an ERROR naming 'mobile pairing rate limiter'; no third limiter. It runs after the mode gate and before the body's code is read; over it → 429 with Retry-After. NO per-instance bucket. The token reaches every API call through the existing seam: components/local-auth-provider.tsx's apiClient.setClerkTokenGetter returns the stored device token (null when none). frontend/lib/api-client.ts does not grow.

A 401 whose code is device_revoked or device_pairing_required clears the stored token and returns to the pairing screen; a paired browser keeps working after a reload and after a server restart (the token is in browser storage, never only in memory).

SaaS, and local with off or open: nothing changes (no discovery-driven screen, no stored token, the same requests as before).

Components under frontend/components/settings/phones-devices/ (≤ 150 lines each; functions ≤ 50), the hook in frontend/hooks/use-mobile-devices.ts, calls only through apiClient (no raw fetch('/api…')), theme tokens only (no dark: palette classes: lib/__tests__/dark-variant-tokens.test.ts guards it).
